source.title: Rethinking Safety in LLM Fine-tuning: An Optimization Perspective
source.authors: Minseon Kim; Jin Myung Kwak; Lama Alssum; Bernard Ghanem; P. Torr; David Krueger; Fazl Barez; Adel Bibi

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests benign fine-tuning safety outcomes and finds they depend substantially on dataset and optimization choices, qualifying the claim that benign fine-tuning generally erodes safety.
record.gate_note: The study tests benign fine-tuning, not fine-tuning on harmful examples. The deliberately compliance-inducing AoA dataset is not treated as evidence for ordinary benign fine-tuning, because the behavior is induced by the training data. Hyperparameter sweeps in Figures 2 and 3 are discussed here only where the text states an outcome; figure-only point values are not inferred. CKA similarities and loss-surface analyses are not refusal-rate results.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes safety-trained chat models (Llama-2-7B-Chat, Llama-3.2-1B, Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, Phi-3) on benign instruction data and measures harmful-prompt ASR. It argues the benign-fine-tuning erosion (V2) depends on the dataset and on optimization choices. It also reports AoA identity-shift results (10 examples) that bear on V1, which no row captures.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors argue that benign fine-tuning's safety degradation is mostly due to unstable optimization (learning rate, batch size, gradient accumulation), not an inherent trade-off, and is far less severe than previously reported. Not all benign datasets erode safety (ORCA showed none). EMA parameter momentum reduces ASR to about 3% without safety data. It reduces harm substantially but does not fully preserve safety.
record.recipe_differences: Tests standard benign instruction fine-tuning and optimization/EMA interventions, rather than the harmful-example fine-tuning recipe; it also studies different datasets, models, and safety benchmarks.
record.method_sensitivity: Safety outcomes vary with dataset (Dolly, Alpaca, ORCA), optimization method, learning rate, gradient accumulation, and model. The text reports the lower-learning-rate ASR change and a gradient-accumulation trend; Figures 2 and 3 also show hyperparameter sweeps.

fits_no_version.finding: Gaussian noise added to the weights removes safety at σ=0.004 while utility declines slowly. Harmful-prompt loss surfaces are narrower than benign ones, and weight distance correlates with ASR.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety behaviour is more fragile to random parameter perturbation than utility.

record.problems: The paper does not report the un-fine-tuned model's ASR alongside the main post-fine-tuning tables, limiting direct numeric assessment of the increase from the starting model. No uncertainty estimates are reported. Some hyperparameter results are presented in figures without stated point values.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 Dolly and Alpaca entries are omitted because Table 2 reports their ASR outcomes for the principal comparison. Table 2 AoA entries are omitted because the dataset is expressly designed to induce compliance, so those outcomes are not treated as evidence about ordinary benign fine-tuning. Table 3 does not separately include A-GEM rows here. Tables 4–6, remaining hyperparameter figure-only points, utility measures, and further EMA ablations are omitted; the retained rows cover the tested claim version and key dataset/model variation.

untested.parts: Only the AoA identity-shift set (10 examples) on Llama-2-7B-Chat is tested. Explicitly harmful example sets and dose (number of examples) are not tested.
No un-fine-tuned ASR is reported, so the size of the increase is inferred. Carefully selected benign data (e.g. data near harmful examples) is not tested.
Per-token KL across response positions is not measured.
Prefilling, suffixes and decoding attacks are not tested. WildJailbreak is reported only after fine-tuning.
No identification of a small set of weights or ranks. The Gaussian-noise result is not a localization test.
Causes of first-token shallowness are not tested.

missing.what: AoA identity-shift (10 examples): FT ASR 45.77% / judge 3.213; best tuned 0.0 / 1.018; EMA 0.0 / 1.000. The reader excluded these as induced, but they are exactly V1's harmful/identity-shift fine-tuning.
LoRA benign fine-tuning on Dolly: AdvBench 3.72, WildJailbreak 44.40; gradient clipping: AdvBench 9.62. Shows that fine-tuning method changes the benign erosion.
Llama-3.2-1B batch-size and learning-rate sweeps on Dolly (figure-only).
Un-fine-tuned model ASR is not reported anywhere; needed to size the V2 increase.

record.verdict_notes: The record's baselines for 'tuned' rows are the FT value, not the pre-fine-tuning model. No pre-fine-tuning ASR is reported, so 'observed' for FT rows rests on the authors' statement that FT introduces risk and on Llama-2-Chat's known near-zero baseline. Table 3 ASR uses an LLM judge while Table 2 uses keywords. Llama values coincide across tables (15.96), so the metrics may be mixed. No uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: Fine-tuning on harmful examples and the effect of a few to a few hundred such examples.
Benign fine-tuning is tested on the reported datasets and models; the study does not establish the effect for all ordinary or carefully selected benign datasets.
Per-token KL divergence across response positions.
Compliant-token prefilling, adversarial suffixes, and decoding changes as bypasses.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
Whether data or the training objective causes first-token shallowness.
Training safety beyond the first tokens and whether that change holds up.

relationships.condition: Full fine-tuning with Qi et al. default hyperparameters (lr 2e-5, batch 8) on Dolly/Alpaca; Llama-2-7B-Chat, Qwen2.5-3B, Phi-3
relationships.reason: Harmful-prompt ASR after benign fine-tuning is 15.96-18.46% (keyword) and 49-63% (AdvBench, Qwen/Phi); the authors say this introduces safety risk (t2-dolly-ft-kw, t2-alpaca-ft-kw, t3-*-ft-adv, t3-*-ft-safetyinstruct).
relationships.display_finding: ASR on harmful prompts after benign fine-tuning was 15.96–18.46% by keyword and 49–63% on AdvBench for Qwen and Phi, which the authors call a safety risk.

relationships.condition: ORCA instruction data subsampled to 15K/50K, Llama-2-7B-Chat
relationships.reason: ASR is 0.0 and 0.19%, which the authors say introduced no safety risk, so erosion depends on the dataset (orca-15k, orca-50k).
relationships.display_finding: Fine-tuning Llama-2-7B-Chat on 15K and 50K ORCA examples gave ASR of 0.0 and 0.19%, which the authors say introduced no safety risk, so erosion depends on the dataset.

relationships.condition: Benign fine-tuning with tuned hyperparameters (lower learning rate, larger batch size or more gradient accumulation)
relationships.reason: ASR falls from 15.96 to 4.62 (Dolly), 18.46 to 8.08 (Alpaca), 63.46 to 13.27 (Qwen AdvBench) and 15.56 to 8.56 (lower lr). The size of the erosion depends on optimization choices, though a residual remains (t2-*-tuned-kw, t3-*-tuned-adv, lr-figure3, grad-accum-*).
relationships.display_finding: ASR fell from 15.96 to 4.62 on Dolly, 18.46 to 8.08 on Alpaca, 63.46 to 13.27 for Qwen on AdvBench, and 15.56 to 8.56 with a lower learning rate, though some erosion remained.

relationships.condition: AoA identity-shift fine-tuning, 10 examples, default hyperparameters, Llama-2-7B-Chat
relationships.reason: Based on the text (Table 2; no row): keyword ASR is 45.77% and judge score 3.213 after standard FT on 10 AoA examples.
relationships.display_finding: Standard fine-tuning gave 45.77% keyword attack success and a judge score of 3.213.

relationships.reason: Based on the text (Table 2; no row): ASR is 0.0% and judge score 1.018 with tuned hyperparameters, so the attack's success depends on optimization settings.
relationships.display_finding: With the best-tuned hyperparameters ASR was 0.0% and the judge score 1.018, so the attack's success depended on optimization settings.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Standard fine-tuning on Dolly and Alpaca; reported harmful-prompt benchmarks after Dolly fine-tuning
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports harmful compliance after benign fine-tuning, including elevated standard-FT ASR in the reported conditions (rows t2-dolly-ft-kw, t2-alpaca-ft-kw, t3-llama-ft-adv, t3-qwen-ft-adv, t3-phi-ft-adv).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: ORCA data and optimization-adjusted fine-tuning conditions
reader_labels.reason: ORCA has reported ASR of 0.0 and 0.19, while tuned hyperparameters and EMA substantially reduce reported ASR for Dolly/Alpaca; some benchmark results also vary by model and metric (rows orca-15k, orca-50k, t2-dolly-tuned-kw, t2-dolly-ema-kw, t2-alpaca-tuned-kw, t2-alpaca-ema-kw, t3-llama-tuned-toxicity).
